Not enough regulation? I think that there was too much state involvement personally. Look at how much better off free market Hong Kong is compared to the rest of China.
Quick question, how does Hong Kong's market differ from Mainland China's in regard to regulation specifically?

Not much difference from the collateral and banking stand point. The big difference was the regulations for starting businesses and working with outside countries.

The problem with their market was too little regulation in that collateral was often the stocks themselves. Which is very similar to the problems America had with housing. Loans were made on houses with the belief that the houses would continue to gain value, when that bubble collapsed the collateral for the loans decreased in value. Thus causing cascading effect. In this case the buying on margin of Chinese stocks is causing a cascading effect as every other stock is getting sold to cover the margins of the borrowers. So not only are the stocks of crappy companies going down, but the stocks of good companies as well.

Here's my story of my first convert:

My father-in-law has been having issues with their Windows Laptop (ASUS) for awhile and I was getting tired of troubleshooting issues over the phone. Finally I asked him, "What do you use your computer for?" and on cue he said "Surfing the web and email". That was all I needed to hear.

I backup the very few documents stored on the machine, formatted the hard drive, and installed Linux Mint KDE. After installing updates, a few applications, and moving all needed icons to the desktop I sent him loose on his new computer. My phone has rang since. He even complained it was too fast now. When I go over to their house I make a point to run updates but that's about it.

What's your story of bringing new people to the Linux Desktop?
Converting Users to the Linux Desktop

My one friend's sister had a shitty old netbook, that could barely run the Windows 7 that came preinstalled on it. She asked me if there was anything I could do to make it usable again. I said I could install linux on it. She didn't like that idea, but then I said, she could either have a non working windows, or a working linux OS. So she agreed.

I installed Elementry OS on it and a few programs she'd need like libre office. I didn't even show her how to use it, and she managed just fine. She said it is way faster, and 2 years later, she still has not had one issue with it.

She mainly uses it for school work, watching series, internet browsing.

Linux is easy to use, if you just bother to spend 5 minutes to learn how the basics work.

Linux is especially good for people who use computer only for basic stuff && if they use non obscure hardware.

E.g. I cannot use Linux for my work full time, because I work with a lot of text and graphics and just a simple copy/paste operation of one "l" from a string like "lll" or pasting something into single or double quotes with a 3px wide I-beam cursor is a nightmare on any Linus DE.

But the shell and text mode editors emacs are great and I use them in VM basically on a daily basis.

I would recommend Linux for internet porn enthusiasts and download junkies who don't have any cash to pay for iTunes or Netflix. It's safer.
